newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's second carrier to lease Boeing jet.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's second carrier to lease Boeing jet.

text.p: Ukraine International Airlines (UIA), the former Soviet republic's second biggest carrier, plans to lease another Boeing jet next month in addition to two leased Boeing planes, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
Company Vice-President Yuri Miroshnykov said the carrier would lease a 150-passenger Boeing 737-400.
UIA, set up in 1992 as a joint venture with Irish aircraft leasing company GPA Group plc, currently operates two leased Boeing 737-200s with 105-passenger capacity each.
"We have no money to buy the plane. But the whole tendency in aviation now is leasing instead of buying because of very high prices for planes," Miroshnykov said by telephone.
He added the third plane would enable UAI to fly daily to Paris and Frankfurt, and to fly five times per week to London.
UIA currently serves 12 western European destinations, including Vienna, Zurich, Berlin, Rome, Brussels and Amsterdam.
Miroshnykov said the company wanted to increase the number of summer charter fligths and to launch a new route to the Crimean peninsula for Western tourists.
Small private Aerosweet carrier is the only other Ukrainian carrier using Western-made planes -- it runs one leased Boeing 737-200.
State-owned Air Ukraine will soon announce the result of a tender between Boeing Corp and Airbus Industrie for planes to replace its Soviet-made Ilyushin 62s on transatlantic routes.
